notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 2 simply supported 50-ft bays, W36X529 girders, one 40-ton cab crane, on column caps over new W14X159 crane columns beside the existing W14X82 building columns (pinned bases, anchor rods and spread footings, crane-level rod X-bracing between the crane columns), with the rail, the top-flange ties and the column ties to the building columns, bearings and end stops; the building columns are checked for the tie forces with their existing load effects and carry no runway vertical load. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.563 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.reason: Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.563 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*).

A jumbo rolled W36X802 (802 lb/ft, 42.6 in deep) passes every girder check of the calculation of this runway built with it (rail-head 0.96, combined 0.79), the screening did not: a heavy alternative, not selected; heavy-shape Charpy and splice rules (AISC 360 A3.1c, to be verified) and mill availability to confirm. No compact W meets every sizing target; the closest: screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 1.45, vertical deflection 0.44, lateral 1.24 and rail-head movement with twist 2.35 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 113 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X487: tips ratio 1.81 > 0.85; …

New crane column for a 40-ton crane (W12X65 to 7.5 t, W14X90 to 15 t, W14X109 to 30 t, else W14X132), pinned base, braced at the cap across the runway by the column tie and along it by the crane-level bracing. The W14X132 crane column does not fit its column cap (validateColumnCap); the lightest heavier W14 that passes.

selections.designed: combined with the building column, 132 in square; 150 in at the braced columns
selections.reason: Isolated 11.5 ft square crane-column footings 34.15 in from the building column would be 64.85 in into its 5 ft footing (6 in clear required): each crane column and its building column stand on one combined footing replacing the existing one, 11 ft square (12.5 ft at the braced columns), the building column shored and re-set on new anchor rods; sized for the base reactions; the braced columns' footing apart from the others' (the rods' uplift and shear along the runway), sliding resisted by the base friction and the soil's lateral bearing on the footing and its shear key (IBC §1806.3.1).

Column tie 0.625 in × 10 in with 3 0.875 in A325 bolts on sleeves in 1.5 in × 2.125 in vertical slots: the lightest within the 0.9 sizing target for the estimated column-tie force 63.336 kip (the girder bottom-flange force through the cap, bounded by the girder tie force estimate 60.463 kip; the crane column's eccentric top reaction 0.187 kip; the brace force 0.01P_r 2.685 kip; the calculation takes the bottom-flange force from the girder model) and its fatigue range 25.401 kip at all cycles; slot travel 0.295 in each way (the larger column shortening plus the erection tolerance).

The building column face from the girder web (the crane-column centerline): at least the crane column's half depth plus the column tie's clear gap, moved out by the tie sizing (to at most 30 in) where the tie needs the flexible length; the crane column stands 19.5 in clear of the building column.

selections.designed: W36X529, closest; plate girder required (rolled W and capped catalogs exhausted)
selections.reason: Plate girder required: no compact rolled W or W and channel cap pair of the catalog meets the girder sizing targets (the closest, W36X529, screening estimates: tips ratio 1.45, vertical deflection 0.44 and lateral 1.24 of the limits against targets 0.85 and 0.9). Design a built-up plate girder with a wide top flange, or shorten the span with intermediate supports; the configurator does not design plate girders. A jumbo rolled W36X802 (802 lb/ft, 42.6 in deep) passes every girder check of the calculation of this runway built with it (rail-head 0.96, combined 0.79), the screening did not: a heavy alternative, not selected; heavy-shape Charpy and splice rules (AISC 360 A3.1c, to be verified) and mill availability to confirm.

selections.designed: paired-bars, closest; tie to be designed by hand
selections.reason: Top-flange tie not resolved: the Paired flat bars on a flange saddle, as sized for the estimated tie demands, still exceeds flange-tie-column 2.91, flange-tie-column-fatigue 2.33, flange-tie-saddle-weld 1.36 (configurator estimates), and no other tie arrangement the configurator tries fits and passes here. Choose another tie or support (a stiffer support), or design the tie connection by hand.

selections.designed: column cap on the W14X159, closest; cap bearing bolts to be designed by hand
selections.reason: Column cap not resolved: on this crane column the calculation gives column-cap-bolt-slip 1.06 for the four 1 in A490 bearing bolts of each girder end at a 7 in gauge (re-sized for the calculated ratios, 1 in A490 at a 8.5 in gauge: column-cap-bolt-slip 1.01, still failing, not taken): the girder model's bottom-flange force exceeds the cap sizing estimates. A 1 1/8 in bolt does not fit this cap: the cap stiffener under the girder bearing stiffener at 7.125 in from grid 2 and its fillets would not land on the column flanges (flange tips 7.8 in). Recommended: a wider crane column (e.g. W14X257) with the larger bolts, a larger bolt with the end bearing re-laid out, or a wider bolt spread or more bolts, designed by hand. The first cap (1 in A490, 7 in gauge) is built and checked.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
